correctness.rationale: Kummer converts each binomial valuation to a borrow count. No admissible proper lower index can be borrow-free because the only subdigit selections are p^s and p^t and neither is divisible by m; k=m p^(t-1) is admissible and has exactly one borrow since m<p. Exhaustive and direct-gcd finite checks corroborate the argument.

originality.rationale: The theorem overlaps known plus/minus-one cases but extends to arbitrary prime residues admitting p^(t-s)=-1 modulo m; in particular the modulus-5 p=2 or 3 residue classes are outside the stated coverage of McTague, Fairfax-Ball, and Wu. Targeted semantic-database and web searches found no equivalent sparse-row statement.
residual_risks: Search is not a proof of historical novelty; unindexed, private, or differently phrased prior work could contain the same sparse-row observation.
Wu's full v2 text was not directly retrievable in this run; its scope comparison relies on its abstract plus Fairfax-Ball's explicit source-level comparison.

value.rationale: The recent p congruent -1 classification leaves natural residue classes untreated. The sparse theorem gives an exact infinite arbitrary-residue family with a short reusable Kummer mechanism, and at modulus 5 it fills both non-+-1 unit classes p congruent 2 and 3 with a precise exponent-gap criterion.
